cases.reason: The term the rule leans on, 'numeric literal', covers a smaller set in 2002. A 2002 floating-point numeric literal has a significand of 1 through 31 digits and an exponent of at most three digits; 2023 allows 36 and four. So MULTIPLY 1.00000000000000000000000000000000E0 BY W-N (33-digit significand) or MULTIPLY 1.0E0001 BY W-N has a literal-1 that is a numeric literal in 2023 and is not one in 2002. The 2002 rule therefore refuses a program the 2023 rule accepts, and the 2023 CONFORMS verdict says nothing about that refusal. The screen did not catch it because the definition lives in 8.3, not in the definitions clause. Probe: --std 2002 compiles both silently (exit 0) and runs (W-N=0002 and W-N=0020). That is a compiler defect at 2002, shared with the 2002 8.3.1.2.2.2 formation rows.
